idiom_name: generic render parameter: impl Fn(&State) -> R
implementation_notes: Rust has no component runtime, so the owner is a hand-written struct or function taking the renderer as a generic bound - fn track<F: Fn(u32, u32) -> R>(render: F) - and the Fn trait documentation states exactly when to use it: accept a parameter of function-like type that is called repeatedly without mutating state, falling back to FnMut or FnOnce when the renderer must mutate or consume its captures. The classic structure is replaced by this generic parameter, or by Box<dyn Fn> when the renderer must be stored in a non-generic type; where a UI framework exists, its children/template props (FnOnce closures) are the same mechanism typed by the framework. Keep the plain generic parameter when the caller composes a closure; move to a framework's prop types when the framework owns the element tree.
pitfalls: Closure captures define the lifetime: a renderer borrowing local state cannot outlive it, so storing it in the owner requires Box<dyn Fn + 'a> or owned captures - the borrow checker will not let a dangling listener survive.
Fn versus FnMut versus FnOnce: a renderer that mutates or consumes its captures needs the weaker bound, and demanding Fn forces consumers into interior mutability (RefCell/Mutex).
dyn storage erases the closure type and blocks inlining; prefer the generic parameter unless type erasure is genuinely required.
